title: Chunking: Visual Guide
outline: 1. The Funnel's Ceiling | IR 202's BM25 + vectors + RRF + reranker funnel on a quality slider, next to an overlap slider that decides whether the sentence at tokens 480-520 survives in any chunk | chunking fixes the unit of indexing and therefore the ceiling: with no overlap the fact is cut, and end-to-end grounding stays 0% however well the funnel is tuned

2. Size Versus Overlap | chunk size and overlap percentage dragged over a 10,000-token document, with vector focus, self-contained passage and index size moving against each other, plus a small-to-big toggle | precision versus completeness is the core tradeoff, chunk count divides by the stride s-o not the size, and a chunk past the embedding model's 512-token cap is truncated without any error

3. Where To Cut | one contract with headings, prose, a 6-row table and a function run through fixed-size, recursive-separator, structure-aware-plus-atomic and semantic splitters at a draggable size limit | fixed splitting cuts tables mid-row and functions mid-body, recursive separators fix prose but not atomicity, and structure-aware splitting keeps atomic units whole and preserves the headers the breadcrumbs need

4. The Distance Spike | the six adjacent-sentence cosine distances 0.11, 0.09, 0.14, 0.58, 0.12, 0.10 against a threshold percentile slider, with an optional min-60/max-120 token cap toggle | semantic boundaries are placed where distance exceeds a percentile of that document's own distribution, so lowering the percentile always makes more and smaller chunks, and the variable-length result still needs size caps that fight each other

5. Breadcrumbs And Context | the same chunk indexed raw, with an Acme MSA breadcrumb, and with an LLM-written 50-100 token context, showing BM25 query-term hits, the 400-contract candidate collapse, the 35% and 49% failure reductions, and prompt-caching cost | enrichment at index time is what repairs the global context splitting destroyed, breadcrumbs are nearly free and deterministic, and prompt caching is what makes per-chunk LLM enrichment affordable
